graph_replay.note: capture on the LARGEST decode case (M=256), replay the M=64 case padded into the same static buffers; both run kernel_id 2005 / opus_moe2_afp8_wfp4_atomic_t32x128x256_sbm32_occ1_cache_b3_ws2, the live decode kernel. `out` is positional arg 6 and is re-zeroed on every fill because the decode path atomically accumulates into it.

math_contract: stage-2 of the a8w4 fused MoE, as ONE segment: out[t,:] = sum_k topk_w[t,k] * (inter_states[t,k,:] @ w2[e(t,k)]^T) with mxfp8 activations x mxfp4 expert weights and e8m0 block scales, scattered through the moe_sorting block map. decode (route_out=False): the down-GEMM atomically accumulates the topk partials directly into a ZEROED out. prefill (route_out=True): the down-GEMM emits per-token-slot partials, then the reduce kernel sums the topk slots into out. Returns the same bf16 [token, model_dim] `out` tensor it was handed (written in place).

tol_note: bf16 output. The decode path (kernel_id 2005) ATOMICALLY accumulates the 6 topk partials into `out`, so the summation order is nondeterministic run-to-run even for the UNTOUCHED baseline: measured on this box the M=1 decode case shows max_rel_err 0.012-0.014 both vs the frozen oracle and baseline-vs-baseline on every random draw, while every other case is bit-exact (0.0). tol=0.05 gives ~3.5x headroom over that measured self-noise and is still 3x tighter than the fp8-output stage-1 head.
